body:
The explicit tracer flux of AdaptiveVerticallyImplicitDiscretization is capped with the total advecting velocity (transport + biogeochemical drift + closure auxiliary velocity + advective forcing), but implicit_step! received only the transport velocities. Above the explicit Courant limit the flux of the drift velocity was therefore silently dropped: a tracer sinking at Courant number 4 descended 15 m instead of 120 m in three steps. The implicit solve now receives the same total velocity as the explicit flux in both the split Runge-Kutta and AB2 steps.

Claude found this bug when I was getting it todo some other stuff and fixed it and seems reasonable to me.

commits.messageBody:
The tapered isopycnal slopes of the advective formulation returned
Union{Float32, Float64} when the grid is Float32 and the closure parameters
are Float64 (the defaults), which crashed the eddy velocity kernel on CUDA.
Convert the slope limiter and minimum_bz to the grid float type in
calc_tapering and isopycnal_slope.

Also add the mutable-grid versions of ∂x_zᶜᶠᶠ and ∂y_zᶠᶜᶠ, and move the
sinking tracer test into the adaptive implicit advection unit tests as a
single-column Courant-4 case.
